semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The term 'lstm' is an abbreviation for 'long short-term memory networks', making it semantically identical to the Given Model.
Both 'long short-term memory networks' and 'lstms' refer to the same type of neural network architecture, thus they are semantically equivalent.

parent_models.justification: Long short-term memory networks (LSTMs) are a specialized type of recurrent neural networks designed to handle dependency problems in sequence prediction.
The term 'recurrent neural network' encompasses several specific architectures, including LSTMs, as they are a type of RNN designed to handle certain limitations in traditional RNNs.
'Simple recurrent neural networks' refers to the basic form of RNNs, under which LSTMs can be categorized as a more advanced variant tackling long-term dependencies.

closest_parent_model.justification: Long short-term memory networks were developed as an improved variant designed to overcome some of the limitations inherent in standard recurrent neural networks, making them the closest parent model.

child_models.justification: The CNN-LSTM combines convolutional layers with LSTM layers, indicating a more specific model under the broader LSTM category.
'Generic cnn-lstm' is a specific implementation involving convolutional and LSTM layers, showing a hybrid model which is a child model of LSTM due to its inclusion of LSTM units.

The CNN-Bi-LSTM-AM model integrates bidirectional LSTMs (a form of LSTM) with convolutional layers and attention mechanisms, which positions it as a specific, specialized child model under the LSTM category.

This model introduces an attention mechanism to LSTMs to enhance the ability of the model to focus on relevant parts of the input sequence, making it a specialized, more specific version of the basic LSTM.

closest_child_model.justification: The CNN-LSTM is a direct extension of simple LSTM models by adding convolutional layers. It is highly relevant and closely tied to the basic function and structure of LSTMs, making it the closest child model.

sibling_models.justification: Though not semantically equivalent to LSTMs, 'second-order recurrent neural networks' fall under the closest parent model of 'recurrent neural networks', making them siblings.
This model can be seen as a different approach within the broader family of RNNs, under which both LSTMs and second-order RNNs fall.
The recurrent attention model, like LSTMs, is an extension of the basic RNN framework focused on improving performance, thus residing under the same overarching category of recurrent neural networks.
A recurrent inference machine is another specific approach within the realm of recurrent neural architectures, sharing the same parent category with LSTMs.
This model is another inventive use of RNNs applied in a specialized domain, thus being a sibling within the recurrent neural network space.

closest_sibling_model.justification: 'Second-order recurrent neural networks' are a significant deviation from standard RNNs to address limitations, similar to LSTMs' purpose. The semantic and functional similarities and differences position it closest to the LSTMs as a sibling model.

unrelated_models.justification: Feed-forward neural networks represent a completely different architecture that does not employ cyclic connections or memory like LSTMs.
Similar to feed-forward neural networks, this deep variant does not relate to LSTM architectures, as it lacks recurrent connections employed in sequence problems.
This model focuses on processes distinctly different from the sequence prediction and memory-focused learning that LSTMs target, indicating no direct relationship.
Wide neural networks do not operate in the sequence prediction domain nor address dependency problems, making them unrelated.
While deep neural networks indicate depth, they are structurally different and are not designed specifically for serial data or dependency management, making them unrelated to LSTMs.
